[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]load, and an operation-count regression gate keeps data-scaled work[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]off the startup path.[/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Reorder the reconcile guards[/bold #D7AFFF]                                  [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]guards[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]guards: reorder `should_reconcile_dead_supervisor` so the cheap [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`monitor_state`/`pid` rejects run before `proc_shell_owns()`, which [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]currently does a full proc-store read for all 147 records when 0 survive[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the next two lines; add a test asserting the proc lookup is skipped for [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]terminal and pid-less records. Measured saving 1.47 s.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Kill the N+1 proc-store reads[/bold #D7AFFF]                                 [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]snapshot[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]snapshot: add a snapshot-scoped proc lookup so `get_proc` stops [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]re-reading and re-parsing the whole store per id, thread one snapshot [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]through the reconcile pass and `_with_proc_projection`, and test that [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]proc-store reads stay bounded regardless of record count.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Stop the O(archive) index query[/bold #D7AFFF]                               [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]bounded-query[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]bounded-query: give reconciliation its own bounded artifact-index query [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]instead of the unbounded full-history `include_hidden` scan of the 115 [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]MB index, leave the `list_monitors` listing path unchanged, and pin the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]new bounds with a test. Escalate to the Rust core if the predicate is [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]not expressible in the existing wire query.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Take reconciliation off the synchronous load[/bold #D7AFFF]                  [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]off-read-path[dim] · [dim][/dim]after guards, snapshot, bounded-query[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]off-read-path: remove the synchronous [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`_reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors_for_tui()` call from [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`_load_agents_from_disk_impl` and run it in the background with a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]coalesced follow-up refresh, reusing the existing loader-cleanup shape, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]while preserving settlement semantics and preventing overlapping passes.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Pin the win with a regression gate[/bold #D7AFFF]                            [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]gate[dim] · [dim][/dim]after off-read-path[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]gate: add a `tests/perf/` bench and baseline asserting bounded [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]proc-store reads and index queries per disk load and no synchronous [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reconciliation, preferring deterministic operation counts over [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]wall-clock seconds, and ask the user before recording the incident in [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the tui_perf memory note.[/#D7D7AF]
